Unsurprisingly, instead of taking action, they launched a campaign which, for thirty years, has derailed the fight against climate change. A shocking investigation uncovers what was done to impede the battle against climate change, and who was behind it.

programme.title: Fred Dibnah's Magnificent Monuments
programme.desc: Steeplejack Fred Dibnah considers the development of castles, from early Iron Age forts to secret underground tunnels used during the Second World War. At Hadrian's Wall, he marvels at the design of Roman toilets, while in Warwick, he joins a band of medieval knights to test the castle's defences.

programme.title: War Walks
programme.desc: A journey through six centuries of warfare in the company of military historian Professor Richard Holmes. In 1415, Henry V won a remarkable victory against a French force that outnumbered him by five to one. Professor Holmes retraces Henry's route to Agincourt and finds a story of heroism and brutality.

programme.title: The Stuarts
programme.desc: Presented by Dr Clare Jackson of Cambridge University, this three-part series argues the Stuarts, more than any other, were Britain's defining royal family. We tend to take today's modern United Kingdom for granted, but there was nothing inevitable about its creation. During the 17th century, the Stuarts grappled with the chaos of three separate Kingdoms, multiple religions and civil war. Britain has not known a century like it and some of the questions this dynasty faced have not gone away. In the opening episode, Clare looks at James VI and I's attempts to unite Scotland and England under the umbrella of his crowns and persuade his subjects to feel more 'British'.

programme.title: Secrets of Size: Atoms to Supergalaxies
programme.desc: In the concluding episode of the series, Jim encounters ever larger cosmic structures to reveal the latest breakthroughs in our understanding of the universe. For example, there’s the heliosphere, a vast cloud of solar plasma that surrounds and protects the solar system. Its unique physics help us understand why life is possible. Larger still, Jim comes face to face with our galactic home the Milky Way, a monstrous structure sculpted by the gravitational forces of dark matter. Jim finds out from pioneering researcher Adrian Fabian about the black hole at its centre, whose strange behaviour includes emitting the lowest note that can be heard in the cosmos. At an even greater scale, Jim encounters huge structures such as the Laniakea Supercluster, of which the Milky Way is only a tiny part. Then there’s 'the giant arc', a collection of galaxies that account for more than three per cent of the observable universe. Jim learns from its discoverer, British PhD student Alexia Lopez, that this gargantuan structure is forcing scientists to reassess their theory of how the universe evolves and may overturn some of the most fundamental principles in physics.

programme.title: Remembers...
programme.desc: One of Britain's most acclaimed and respected directors, Ken Loach, is the man behind award-winning films like The Wind that Shakes the Barley, Land and Freedom and I, Daniel Blake - but in terms of impact, his most important piece will for many always be the BBC's 1966 television drama Cathy Come Home. Written by Jeremy Sandford, produced by Tony Garnett and with Carol White in the titular role, Cathy's look at the plight of Britain's homeless left viewers shocked and forced the nation to confront an issue that until then had largely been ignored. Here, Ken looks back on the experiences of making the film, and shares his insights into the reactions it generated. Critics like Mary Whitehouse attacked him and the BBC for abandoning impartiality and brainwashing the public, while others applauded a groundbreaking and important piece of campaigning drama.

programme.title: In Conversation
programme.desc: Actor Cillian Murphy, who played the lead role in Ken Loach's Palme d'Or-winning film The Wind That Shakes the Barley, talks to the director at the BFI Southbank about a prolific career dedicated to documenting social and political injustice, the importance of artistic collaboration, the often-overlooked humour in Loach's films, and the impact working with Loach had on his own approach to acting.

programme.title: Mark Kermode's Secrets of Cinema
programme.desc: Mark Kermode explores one of the most distinctive and popular genres of all. The spy movie plays on our paranoia and feeds our fears as well as fulfilling our fantasies of secret missions and special skills. It has also given us perhaps the most famous hero in all of cinema – James Bond. Spy movies capture a world not of black and white but shades of grey. But if the morality is often ambiguous, the genre is full of tried and tested conventions. Mark opens up the cinematic agent’s essential toolkit, from the spy boss to the mysterious McGuffin, surveillance techniques to a striking set of opening titles, and he traces the development of the genre from its earliest days. Whether you’re a blockbuster superspy or a compromised cold warrior, Mark reveals all you need to survive in the murky yet thrilling world of big screen espionage.

programme.title: In Conversation
programme.desc: Actor Cillian Murphy, who played the lead role in Ken Loach's Palme d'Or-winning film The Wind That Shakes the Barley, talks to the director at the BFI Southbank about a prolific career dedicated to documenting social and political injustice, the importance of artistic collaboration, the often-overlooked humour in Loach's films, and the impact working with Loach had on his own approach to acting.

programme.title: Timeshift
programme.desc: What happens when a literary novelist tries to write popular romantic fiction? To mark 100 years of romance publishers Mills and Boon, literary novelist Stella Duffy takes on the challenge of writing for them. Romantic fiction is a global phenomenon, and Mills and Boon are among the biggest names in the business. The company welcomes submissions from new authors, but as Duffy soon finds out, writing a Mills and Boon is harder than it looks. Help is at hand from the publishers themselves, a prolific Mills and Boon author and some avid romance fans, as Duffy's quest to create the perfect romantic novel takes her from London to Italy on a journey that is both an insight into the art of romantic fiction and the joy and frustration of writing itself.

programme.title: Girls in Bands at the BBC
programme.desc: Compilation celebrating some guitar band performances at the BBC that feature some of the best female musicians in rock. Beginning with the oft-forgotten American group Fanny performing You're the One, it's a journey along rock's spectrum from the 1970s to now. The selection includes the powerful vocals of Elkie Brooks on Vinegar Joe's Proud to Be a Honky Woman, the mesmerising poetry of Patti Smith's Horses and the upbeat energy of The Go-Go's on We Got the Beat. Mighty basslines come courtesy of Tina Weymouth on Psycho Killer and Kim Gordon on Sugar Kane, whilst we trace the line of indie rock from the Au Pairs through Lush, Elastica and Garbage to current band Savages.

programme.title: AI Decoded
programme.desc: Would you let AI walk around your home? We explore the growing race to put humanoid robots into our homes and workplaces. We examine Meta's reported robot project, the rise of Chinese robot manufacturers, the privacy risks of machines that can see, hear and map our lives and whether robots are becoming Big Tech's next multi-trillion-dollar bet. Meta has reportedly built a humanoid robot called Max and, if Mark Zuckerberg gets his way, this could be the next frontier for artificial intelligence. After years of AI living on our screens, Silicon Valley is now racing to give AI a body, one that can see, hear, move through the world and interact with people in real life. Could a humanoid robot really become as common as a smartphone? Would you trust one to help around the house, care for an elderly relative, or perform tasks at work? And as companies spend hundreds of billions of dollars on AI, are robots the breakthrough the industry has been waiting for, or another expensive gamble destined to disappoint?

Just like old times, eh Tommy!

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Join Natasha Raskin Sharp for this hunt, which sees a rare edition of a Harry Potter book go under the hammer with a spellbinding estimate. programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: Jacqui Joseph is in Buckinghamshire, determined to stop quality items being crushed at High Wycombe recycling centre. She sees potential in a drop-leaf table, a collection of canvas frames and a monk's bench, and enlists the help of upcycler Tristan Merriam and woodworker Martin Hough to try to bring them back to their best. Will Jacqui succeed in sending all three revamped items off to new homes?

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: The focus is firmly on Wiltshire today as Jonnie Irwin helps a couple from London with a £550k budget to make a life-changing rural move to this beautiful county. Jonnie also meets a group of bicycling enthusiasts, joining them on a ride through the fascinating Longleat Estate.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Elegant Elaine is first through the doors, making friends wherever she goes. But will her miniature perfume bottles bring the sweet smell of success? Next up is local lad Alex, selling a shop sign of dubious provenance. It’s a commercial lot, but a lack of age means it might struggle to bring in big money. Third to face the dealers is Daniel from London, with a very unusual pair of fur-covered bedside tables. Nigel and Simon may be baffled, but Daniel puts a hefty price tag on what is definitely a unique offering. Whether that’s a good or a bad thing remains to be seen. Next up is Janet, with her Egyptian revival door knocker, although she seems more interested in taking one of the dealers home than making any money. Ian, though, is in denial. Glamorous Pixie LeBon comes in last, with a Second World War wedding dress made out of parachute silk. It’s a museum-quality piece of social history, but will that value translate into bids from the dealers?

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Jacqui, Harry, Annie and Andrew – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie, and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.desc: A celebration of 30 years of the MOBO organisation. A defining milestone for black British music and culture, this landmark anniversary looks at the history of the awards, its ambition, cultural impact and legacy, and features some of the awards' most iconic moments and memorable performances.

programme.title: The Famous Finish Line
programme.desc: Quiz show hosted by Roman Kemp with sidekick Sarah Greene. Five celebrities - Rick Edwards, Harley Moon Kemp, Mollie Pearce, Molly Rainford and La Voix - race in moving podiums across a star-spangled-themed studio to try to win £10,000 for their chosen charity. Correct answers get the celebrities moving, while wrong ones stop them in their tracks. They must battle across a series of fast-paced qualifiers and head-to-head races, where the aim of the game is simple - make it to the finish line before your rivals. The winner then races against the track itself in an attempt to win the £10,000 cash prize for their chosen charity.

The van's camera captures the devastating impact, and a witness recounts the shocking aftermath. On another country road, a risky overtake brings a car face-to-face with a lorry. An insurer untangles a disputed roundabout crash, while tests in Caerphilly reveal the terrifying forces unleashed in a collision.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: A developer in East Sussex wants to add an extra floor onto a three-storey building, but will he be successful? A mum of four is tackling a project in Dorset with the help of relatives. Another family affair in Derbyshire involves sorting out some serious-looking cracks.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Today’s show comes from a bustling antiques fair in Detling in Kent, where two teams browse jam-packed stalls with the aim of buying three items in an hour to take to auction. The red team, friends Bill and Al, known as Del Boy and Rodney to their friends, are led around by expert Catherine Southon, while the blues, performing arts teachers Jo and Simisola, are treated to the dry wit of expert Mark Stacey. Both teams browse a variety of items, but whereas the blues finish with enough time to grab a cuppa, the reds take it right to the wire. With the seconds counting down, Bill, Al and Catherine desperately try to find their third item. Will they do a deal in time? Presenter Eric Knowles visits the Kent Museum of the Moving Image to learn about peep boxes and magic lanterns, two early forms of visual entertainment that delighted audiences as far back as the 17th century. Over in Portsmouth, auctioneer Daniel Tricker is doing the business on the rostrum.

Tommy is in London on the peninsula of the Isle of dogs, where a three-bedroom flat has great potential as a development opportunity.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: In this special episode, four well-known Radio DJs go head-to-head at one of Britain’s biggest antiques fairs to raise money for charity. Hoping to spin loads of profits are BBC Radio 2’s OJ Borg and his teammate Melvin Odoom opposite BBC Asian Network’s Nikita Kanda and Radio 1’s Maia Beth. Let’s hope their antiques experts Izzie Balmer and Nick Hall are on the same wavelength as they hunt for bargains among the stalls. A brass pipe sparks a conversation about foreign languages for the reds, but are they speaking the right lingo when it comes to negotiating a good price on some Scandinavian jewellery? Across the fair, Nikita and Maia take a shine to a tatty footstool in the form of a bulldog, but Nick doubts it has any pedigree, and the musical blues compose their own Bargain Hunt song as they try to drum up a profit. At the auction in Chippenham, Izzie confounds her team with a Japanese bonus buy, while Nick hopes his will take off with the bidders.

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: The Northumbria Mysteries
programme.desc: When estate agent Luke Wandle is found brutally murdered in his own office, Rose and Raj are met with a tangled web of motives. Naturally, suspicion falls on the two people who discovered the body: Luke’s wife, Catherine, and his business partner Damon. But as the investigation deepens, the suspect list rapidly expands to include an embittered former employee with an axe to grind, and Luke’s tight-lipped secretary and her controlling husband, all hiding secrets of their own.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: A couple from the Surrey town of Epsom enjoy the spectacular landscape in Argyll and Bute as Nicki Chapman provides them with some expert property advice. For their budget of £600,000, they want a house with views that just keep on giving. Nicki also takes to the water on Loch Lomond to meet a family who have owned and lived on an island for 70 years.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Looking to mix things up is Sarah, bearing an impressive silver-plated lighthouse-shaped cocktail shaker. She’s brought her own Elvis impersonator to woo the dealers, but she might get even more help from our very own Nigel Havers. Jason continues to bring the bling, with a uranium glass jewellery set that radiates class. He clearly has a great eye, but will the dealers share his taste? Third to face the dealers is Kamran from Bradford. He’s got a papal artefact he found in the attic, and backed up by some diligent research, he’s looking to move it on. Clayton doesn’t know much about his jade disc, but that just means it might be a sleeper hit. So, will he be able to earn a pretty penny on this charity shop find? Smoking may be bad for your health, but selling smoking memorabilia can be good for your bank balance. Danni’s stylish cigar cutters certainly fit the bill, but the buyers will have to work hard, as she won’t let them go for a snip.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the high-stakes quiz as a team of soap stars, featuring EastEnder Danielle Harold, Hollyoaks’s Lucy-Jo Hudson, Coronation Street’s Simon Gregson and Emmerdale’s Chris Bisson, get together to take on the Bridge of Lies for their chosen charities. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and 10 lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money, step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge, they just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash for their chosen charities.

programme.title: Pointless
programme.desc: Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Vick Hope for the brainy quiz where the contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

programme.title: BBC News at Six
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: BBC London
programme.desc: The latest news, sport and weather from London.

programme.title: BBC Children in Need
programme.desc: BBC Children in Need brings the nation together for a spectacular evening of entertainment, warmth and sparkle, with more than a sprinkle of Hollywood stardust. Live from MediaCityUK in Salford, hosts Mel Giedroyc, Sara Cox, Alex Jones, Rylan and Tyler West lead a star-studded show packed with famous faces, dazzling performances, exclusive sketches and big surprises. Highlights on the night include special collaborations with much-loved BBC shows, plus the heartwarming return of the Children in Need Choir, who sing a special medley live. The One Show Challenge Squad take centre stage again as new recruits Zoe and Serena tackle epic challenges to help make a difference to other young lives. Radio 2's Owain Wyn Evans is live in the studio for a hero's welcome after completing his gruelling 400-mile four nations cycle challenge in aid of this year’s appeal. Alongside the glitz and glamour, inspiring stories from children and young people across the UK highlight the life-changing impact of BBC Children in Need.

programme.title: BBC London

programme.title: The Graham Norton Show
programme.desc: Together on Graham's sofa are award-winning Wicked star Cynthia Erivo, in the film version of hit play Prima Facie; Time star David Tennant, talking about the new season of Rivals; triple Oscar nominee Laura Linney, in moving British romantic drama Onwards and Sideways; and top comic Rob Brydon, returning to the world of sitcom in Bill's Included. With music from Noah Kahan, performing The Great Divide, the title track of his current album.

programme.title: The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes
programme.desc: Years before he becomes the tyrannical president of Panem, 18-year-old Coriolanus Snow remains the last hope for his fading lineage. With the tenth annual Hunger Games fast approaching, the young Snow becomes alarmed when he is assigned to mentor Lucy Gray Baird from District 12. Putting together their instincts for showmanship and political savvy, they race against time to ultimately reveal who is a songbird and who is a snake.

programme.title: Chloe Ayling: My Unbelievable Kidnapping
programme.desc: Chloe Ayling is kidnapped at a fake modelling shoot in Milan. When the police learn she’s due to be auctioned as a sex slave, a major investigation begins.

programme.title: Chloe Ayling: My Unbelievable Kidnapping
programme.desc: Kidnapped and held in a remote farmhouse, and with Black Death’s auction looming, Chloe realises she must find a way to gain control over her captor.

programme.title: Chloe Ayling: My Unbelievable Kidnapping
programme.desc: Glamour model and kidnapping victim Chloe Ayling continues to look back at her terrifying ordeal orchestrated by Black Death. Now safely under the protection of the Italian authorities, she must give evidence in court against the man who enabled her escape from the international sex-trafficking gang – Lukasz Herba. But as the hearing starts and the evidence is laid out, a different picture begins to emerge of this particular suspect. Dazed from the shock of this discovery, Chloe returns home to the UK, finally free of the spectre of a gang she believed could continue to threaten her life. Whilst now free from one unimaginable ordeal, she’s immediately plunged into another as the Italian courts publicly release details of the case and the ongoing investigation to the world’s press. What she hoped to bury as an embarrassing nightmare soon ignites the interest of the global media. Now they know her name and discover where she lives.

programme.title: Top Gear
programme.desc: Jeremy Clarkson, Richard Hammond and James May take an Aston DBS Volante, a Ferrari California and a Lamborghini Gallardo Spyder to Romania in search of an obscure stretch of tarmac that some hardcore drivers claim is nothing less than the greatest road in the world. Meanwhile, James makes a rare appearance on the track as he compares two absurdly powerful limos, the BMW 760i and Mercedes S63 AMG, and gets into a strange card game with the Stig. Star Trek, Troy and Hulk star Eric Bana is the Hollywood legend in the Reasonably Priced Car.

programme.title: BBC New Comedy Awards
programme.desc: The BBC's biggest comedy talent search is heading to Coventry, where five comics will compete in the second of six knockout heats to bag their place in the grand final.

programme.desc: 1593. While King Philip of Spain plots to kill Queen Elizabeth of England, young Bill Shakespeare leaves Stratford to follow his latest dream, to be a playwright in London - despite the theatres being closed due to plague. Luckily the Queen desires a new play - unluckily she chooses creepy Lord Crawley to write it.

programme.desc: The doors of Slane Castle have opened once again, with 23 new players entering The Traitors Ireland for its second season. Hosted once again by Siobhán McSweeney, the players attempt to navigate a game built on trust, strategy and deception, forming alliances while trying to work out who among them they can believe.

programme.desc: Rising journalist Alison Scott's career hits a serious bump in the road after a one-night stand with irresponsible slacker Ben Stone results in pregnancy. Rather than raise the baby on her own, she decides to give Ben a chance to prove he is father material. However, he is unsure if he is ready, and both wonder if they would be compatible lifetime partners.

programme.title: Stacey Dooley
programme.desc: Rehab centres are treating some of their youngest-ever and most physically damaged addicts, and ketamine has been their drug of choice. Stacey Dooley gains rare access to a rehab in Stockport and gets to know former users. Many are in chronic pain, and one young man needs bladder reconstruction surgery. Over four months, she follows them through recovery, relationships, setbacks and celebrations.

programme.title: Stacey Dooley
programme.desc: Stacey follows three Ukrainian civilians training with British soldiers to fight Russia. In just five weeks, a florist, a welder and a jeweller learn to 'survive and be lethal'.

programme.title: My Mate's a Bad Date
programme.desc: Khalil never remembers his dates’ names, so he calls them all 'baby girl' to skirt around it. Obsessed with looking good, he checks himself out in the reflection of a spoon every 20 minutes on dinner dates and thinks it’s impressive to tell boastful, drunken stories. No wonder the ladies don’t come back for a second date! Cavan is fed up of his best mate Khalil’s dating fails and Khalil not listening to his advice, so he calls on the help of Gen Z's most trusted sex and relationships expert, Oloni, to put this 21-year-old Notts boy on the spot and get him to own up to his bad dating habits. Khalil and Oloni watch video feedback from some very honest friends and exes to show him first hand where it's all going wrong, before Oloni sets Khalil up on a series of first dates that will challenge him to turn him from a bad date to a good date. Under the watchful eye of Oloni and Cavan, can Khalil stop calling his dates 'baby girl', can he resist the urge to check himself out and will he take Oloni's advice on board and stop telling laddish, drunken stories?

programme.title: My Mate's a Bad Date
programme.desc: Larisa is fed up of hearing about her best mate Dami’s latest in a long line of dating fails. He walks out mid-date, interrogates and pulls girls up on their outfits, music choices and lifestyle, and thinks they’re lucky to have him! It’s time for an intervention, so Larisa enlists the help of Gen Z’s most trusted sex and relationships expert Oloni to put the 24-year-old Londoner on the spot and help him own up to his disastrous dating habits. Oloni reviews his dating past and gives him a cold, hard dose of reality as she and Dami watch some honest and sometimes surprising video feedback from family members, friends and even exes to show him where it’s all going wrong. Oloni sets Dami up on a series of first dates that will challenge him to shake off his bad habits and hopefully become a better dater. As Oloni and Larisa watch on, can Dami ditch the interrogation act, stop being so rude to his dates and actually stay to the end?

programme.title: BBC Comedy Short Films
programme.desc: Calamity James is a slapstick comedy about a young man, James, who is cursed with ‘acute misfortune syndrome’. James tries to reconnect with his dad after being thrown out by his mum for setting fire to their house at a family barbecue. In this world, chronic bad luck exists and the unbelievable is the everyday.

programme.desc: Twenty-five-year-old Mancunian Tyler is a self-confessed serial dater who treats dating like a sport and goes on five or six dates a week. She’s rude and sarcastic, rambles on about herself, gets bored easily and doesn’t stay focused on her dates. Best mate Yazmine is sick of hearing about Tyler’s dating disasters. Tyler needs help, so Yazmine calls on Gen Z’s most trusted sex and relationships expert, Oloni, to kick-start an intervention. Oloni pulls Tyler up on her catastrophic dating habits and delivers some tough truths as she and Tyler watch frank video feedback from friends and exes to prove to Tyler that there needs to be a change. Oloni has her job cut out with this one and sets Tyler up on three challenge dates as she and Yazmine watch on. Tyler insists her ideal date is the male version of herself, but will the male ‘Tyler’ be the perfect match for this feisty female?

programme.title: Wallace & Gromit: A Close Shave
programme.desc: Oscar-winning claymation comedy thriller from Nick Park, featuring the popular inventor and his dog. Wallace's whirlwind romance with the proprietor of the local wool shop puts his head in a spin, and Gromit is framed for sheep rustling in a fiendish criminal plot, meeting a sheep named Shaun along the way. Will Wallace snap out of his daze in time to rescue his canine companion?

programme.title: Wallace & Gromit: The Wrong Trousers
programme.desc: Oscar-winning animated adventure featuring Wallace and Gromit. The duo are plunged into a hilarious tale of skulduggery involving an extraordinary pair of automated trousers and a villainous penguin. Featuring Peter Sallis as the voice of Wallace.

programme.title: Beyond Paradise
programme.desc: Humphrey and his team are baffled by a set of reverse burglaries where items are left behind rather than taken. With their only credible suspect being Santa, it’s a race against time to find the real culprit in time for Christmas. The only clues are a pile of ash and glove fibres at each location. With four open cases counting against them, and police HQ breathing down their necks, the team are up against it. They must figure out how the victims are connected, catch the person responsible and save the station in time for the festivities. But when the team make a breakthrough with an unexpected connection to 1973, it’s a bittersweet discovery that makes them reconsider the true meaning of Christmas.

programme.title: Beyond Paradise
programme.desc: Whilst home alone watching family videos, Bob encounters a surprise visitor - his late wife’s ghost, Linda, who has a haunting demand: get out. When there’s a second unsettling encounter and writing on a mirror, Humphrey and the team are called in to investigate. Esther is deeply sceptical, but Humphrey is more than happy to dive into his first haunting. Surely there’s a rational explanation?

programme.title: Mrs Brown's Boys
programme.desc: It may be a time for peace and goodwill, but there is trouble brewing in the Brown household this Christmas. Cathy takes exception to having her mother opening her mail and instigates a clever plan for revenge. Agnes is shocked when the annual Nativity play is cancelled. She vows to stage her own Christmas play. The new priest puts his foot down - but nobody gets in the way of Agnes Brown.

programme.title: Mrs Brown's Boys
programme.desc: Agnes Brown has finally been given permission to stage her own Nativity play and is determined to put on the greatest show on Earth. The only thing standing in her way now is local priest Father Damien, who is insisting that Agnes makes some last-minute changes to her rather unusual script. Will Agnes ever get to play the Virgin Mary?

programme.title: A Cock and Bull Story
programme.desc: An imaginative and witty adaptation of Laurence Sterne's 'unfilmable' novel The Life and Opinions of Tristram Shandy, Gentleman. Tristram Shandy, played by Steve Coogan, guides viewers through the epic tale of his life and opinions, chopping back and forth in time, commenting on his tale as he tells it.

programme.title: Ghosts Christmas Special
programme.desc: It’s coming up to Christmas, and Mike’s mum is staying. Betty wants to be helpful, but it isn’t long before she is driving Mike and Alison round the bend. Betty has overstayed her welcome, but Alison and Mike don’t quite have the heart to tell her. Just as she decides to leave of her own volition, Betty suspects something is terribly wrong at Button House. She adopts extreme measures to make the house safe and in doing so endangers the resident Ghosts – will they come out of this unscathed?

programme.title: A Course Called Ireland
programme.desc: After a hair-raising drive across the Conor Pass and a spot of seaside silliness hitting golf balls into the ocean, Bill bids farewell to Chris O'Dowd. In County Clare, Bill and Tom's attempt to sneak unnoticed into a hurling match goes awry, before an emotional reunion recalls an unforgettable act of kindness. Then, a chance invitation in Ballybunion leads to a freezing Atlantic challenge.

programme.title: MasterChef: The Professionals
programme.desc: Six ambitious chefs enter the MasterChef kitchen ready to prove they have what it takes to succeed in the competition. Across two demanding challenges, they’ll need to demonstrate their skills.

programme.title: Rise of the Rockstar Chef
programme.desc: Marco Pierre White's meteoric rise opening Harvey's and how the unpredictable young genius took fledgling Gordon Ramsay under his wing as a young Heston Blumenthal began his career.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Christina is rudely awakened to present this episode from Taunton in Somerset, where a huge antiques centre beckons for two teams of shoppers. In red are friends Aimi and Neil, and in blue are siblings Joe and Bella. With expert Ben Cooper by their side, the reds wonder whether they can cut a deal with an old knife box, while the blues and Danny Sebastian ponder over a wooden propeller – but aerospace engineer Joe doesn’t think it’ll fly at auction. In neighbouring Wiltshire, Christina visits the historic town of Malmesbury to learn about its ancient royal connections. In the abbey, she sees the tomb of the first king of England, Æthelstan, and pops next door to the Old Bell Hotel, which has been welcoming guests since 1220, including King Henry III in 1265. The hotel is now owned by a Texan businessman who has a surprising family connection to the guesthouse. At auction in nearby Chippenham, can auctioneer Tim Weeks make some right royal profits for the reds and blues?

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martin is impressed by the use of space at a West Midlands terrace. Dion is in Salford, where less might be more with a project. The opposite is true with three flats on offer in Croydon, as it requires deep pockets to bring them back to life.

programme.title: The Reluctant Vampire
programme.desc: The day of Val’s initiation ceremony approaches, and he still has no idea how he’ll pass the vampire test. When his final plan doesn’t work out, he realises he can no longer live a double life and is faced with the ultimate dilemma. Should he come clean and risk everything for the chance of a human life or sacrifice who he really is for the sake of his family?

programme.title: Only Connect
programme.desc: Victoria Coren Mitchell hosts the quiz where knowledge only gets you so far – the vital extra ingredients are logic and lateral thinking. There’s an EastEnders-style revelation as a family team face three former work colleagues, all trying to find connections between such apparently random clues as Kite’s Nest, Ravenseat, Duchy Home and Diddly Squat.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Politics Live
programme.desc: The big political issues of the day.

programme.title: Impossible
programme.desc: Game show in which 24 players compete across the series, scoring points by answering questions correctly. However, they must avoid the Impossible answers, otherwise they will be eliminated from the show until the next day. In each episode, there are three rounds, and the three highest scorers from each round play against each other in the final. The winner of this battle faces a £10,000 question.

programme.title: The Answer Run
programme.desc: Comedian Jason Manford hosts an exciting, fast-paced quiz show, where three couples face a series of 50/50 questions which hurtle The Answer Run down towards them. Across three rounds, the couples build up their cash pots, but only one pair can face The Final Run and win the chance to take home their cash prize. Who will swipe their way to victory?

programme.title: Dunkirk (1958)
programme.desc: In 1940, more than 338,000 men were taken off Dunkirk beach in an operation that became legendary. This epic film recreates the event.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel and the team visit Dartington Hall near Totnes in Devon. Among the items brought to light are a set of royal cufflinks and a letter from Admiral Nelson.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Today Flog It! comes from Huddersfield Town Hall in West Yorkshire. Our experts Nick Davies and Christina Trevanion are on hand to find a selection of objects to take to auction. Nick is drawn to a bobbin holder that reveals the town’s textile heritage, while Christina finds an incredible collection of glass scent bottles. Paul Martin delves into the area’s coal mining history with a journey deep underground at the National Coal Mining Museum for England.

programme.title: House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Dame Laura Kenny, Minah Shannon, Seann Walsh and Ricky Wilson take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, Michael Sheen. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted with the House of Games record player?

programme.title: Strictly - It Takes Two
programme.desc: Ellie Taylor is back with an exclusive first look at how some of the celebs are getting on with their next dances. Strictly judges Shirley Ballas and Anton Du Beke drop in for a chat.

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Paul and Bob venture to the northernmost reaches of the UK – Shetland – to fish the lochs and the seas of this remote and beautiful place for trout and pollock. Shetland is an archipelago of about 100 islands off the north east coast of Scotland, only around 15 of which are inhabited. It feels like they have entered a very different world - and it's full of surprises for both of them.

programme.title: The Future with Hannah Fry
programme.desc: With the promise of unimaginable computing power, a global race for quantum supremacy is raging. Hannah Fry looks inside the IBM research facility, one of the oldest tech companies in the world, to uncover the future of quantum technology. She explores the unprecedented potential of quantum computing and how precarious this advanced power may be in the wrong hands. Through her exclusive interviews with world-class experts in quantum technologies, Hannah explores the international quantum arms race between the US and China. She breaks down the implications of this 21st-century race and how a quantum future could change the very nature of humanity.

programme.title: The Secret Genius of Modern Life
programme.desc: Hannah takes a look at the air fryer – a device that is rapidly taking over people's kitchens, cooking up everything from bread rolls to baked Alaska and almost making ovens obsolete. Hannah dives into its surprising history, going behind the scenes with air fryer originators Philips. She discovers how the accidental creation of a wonder wire in the 1900s, a WWII pilot’s cold dinner and one man tinkering in his garage created this modern marvel that is redefining cooking.

programme.title: The Repair Shop
programme.desc: The team restore a Man Utd shirt worn by a Busby Babe in the FA Cup final, a Bible from a wartime internment camp, an ornate Punjabi hookah and a Bradford shop window automaton.

programme.title: Murder in Belfast: Sisters Seeking Justice
programme.desc: Police believe they are closer to catching Robert’s killers, but they have to contend with the fact that some witnesses have also been talking to the IRA. As the political ramifications of the murder settle, a trial finally looms and Robert’s family hope that their years of battling have put justice in reach.

programme.title: QI
programme.desc: Sandi Toksvig samples some X-themed materials. With Zoe Lyons, Susan Calman, Laura Smyth and Alan Davies.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the news stories of the day. With Victoria Derbyshire.

programme.title: Unspun World with John Simpson
programme.desc: John Simpson, in discussion with the BBC's unparalleled range of experts across the world, explores how the results of the US midterm elections are reshaping American politics, analyses what the latest UN climate summit can achieve, and looks at how young criminals are being hired to carry out arson and murder in Europe.

programme.title: Mums v Big Pharma
programme.desc: Two mums from north west England tell the story, based on their experience, of taking on a drugs company, doctors and the government, fighting a scandal that led to at least 20,000 babies being born disabled - the truly shocking scandal of sodium valproate. The film reveals, for the first time, the ‘David v Goliath’ battle as they search for answers and fight for justice for their children.

programme.title: MasterChef: The Professionals
programme.desc: The remaining five chefs return to the kitchen for two demanding challenges that will push their skills, creativity and ambition to the limit as they battle for a place in the quarter-final.

programme.title: Eva Longoria: Searching for France
programme.desc: Sitting between Germany and France, Alsace is frontier land with a cuisine to match. In Strasbourg, Eva stops off at Brasserie Le Tigre for a beer (brassier means ‘to brew’) and a deliciously creamy tarte flambee. Then there's a trip to guide Coralie Andt’s restaurant, known as a winstub, where French wines can be enjoyed with plenty of cheese and sausage – as well as more sausage with sauerkraut cooked in white Riesling wine. With French tarts in a brasserie that serves German-style beer, and German sausage in a winstub serving French white wine, Alsace is defined by its competing national influences.

programme.desc: Wooden shoe lasts are a common sight at antiques fairs, but do you know how they’re made? Natasha Raskin Sharp visits the workshop of cordwainer Payson Muller, originally a stonemason, who turned his talents to making bespoke shoes on hand-carved shoe lasts. He creates them from beech boughs before refining their shape using a knife and rasp. Hoping to cut a few deals of their own are two teams of bargain hunters, shopping for collectibles at Wetherby Racecourse. In blue are couple Martin and Nasreen, and their opponents are married duo Lisamarie and Jamie. Nasreen’s keen eye spots an ornate Russian caviar bowl and spoon, but the price tag is an eye-watering £600. Elsewhere, Jamie comes across a wacky glass vase that resembles a famous artist’s work, but Philip Serrell thinks it’s no masterpiece. At the sale, both teams hope for big profits, but all they can do is watch as their items go under auctioneer Caroline Hawley’s hammer.

Autumn is a busy time with vegetables to sow, perennials to plant and windfall apples to collect. Carol Klein takes a deep dive into the scientific world of plants. This time, it’s all about the magical properties of their shoots. Joe Swift visits close friend and garden designer Ann-Marie Powell to explore her own garden, a place that has become her solace since the death of her husband last year. In North Yorkshire, there’s a remarkable, pioneering woman on a quest to grow thousands of trees from seed. And a couple in East Grinstead share their combined love for the garden they have created together.

We meet a keen collector of battlefield finds known as trench art, and the finest music box to appear on the Roadshow is valued.

Paul Martin is joined by experts Christina Trevanion and Mark Stacey. Together the team pick out a selection of interesting antiques and collectables to be sold at the local auction house. Christina uncovers a famous fake while Mark gets a religious education after discovering a rare Baptist bust. Paul delves into the history of the auction site which is built on top of infamous Greenham Common.

programme.title: The Future with Hannah Fry
programme.desc: Humanity's very survival depends on water. But global reserves are rapidly shrinking with no end in sight thanks to unmitigated climate change, population growth and poor resource management. Over two-thirds of the global population are faced with water stress, while millions have already been displaced by intense water scarcity which is now replacing oil as the most likely cause of global conflict. Hannah Fry learns about the different ways in which technology could help secure humanity’s future water needs. She witnesses the effects of water scarcity in Kenya and learns about how technological solutions are currently being harnessed to reverse this dire situation.

programme.title: The Secret Genius of Modern Life
programme.desc: Fridges have been quietly ‘keeping things cool’ in the kitchen for over 100 years, and yet most of us barely give them a second thought. Hannah hits the production line with appliance giants Bosch to find the lifeblood at the heart of every fridge and gets a lesson in carrot droop. And she takes a long, cool look at the fridge’s history to reveal how a French monk with a flair for chemistry, a 17th century chicken incubator and an explosive invention in Australia created the ultimate chill.

programme.title: Monty Don’s British Gardens
programme.desc: Monty Don explores the most densely populated part of the country, London and the home counties. He visits some of London’s gardens, including a special one on a barge, as well as a beautifully restored garden close to where he grew up in Hampshire and some gardens known for their different and personal styles of planting.

programme.title: Rise of the Rockstar Chef
programme.desc: Marco chases three Michelin stars, Gordon breaks away to build his own name, and Heston rewrites the rules as huge success brings both fame and a new world of pressure.

programme.title: Cunk on Cinema
programme.desc: Philomena Cunk’s groundbreaking history of cinema begins. Cunk meets Hollywood legends and interrogates the writer of Die Hard, as she starts her quest deep, deep into cinema. She witnesses the shockingly poor picture quality of the earliest films and marvels at the beards of their Victorian inventors; she gasps audibly at the invention of sound; and she critiques some of the supposedly finest creations of Hollywood’s Golden Age. Along the way she interviews filmmakers, actors and critics, including several you’ve definitely heard of, and she (and you) finally discovers the true meaning of The Wizard of Oz.

programme.title: The Future with Hannah Fry
programme.desc: With the promise of unimaginable computing power, a global race for quantum supremacy is raging. Hannah Fry looks inside the IBM research facility, one of the oldest tech companies in the world, to uncover the future of quantum technology. She explores the unprecedented potential of quantum computing and how precarious this advanced power may be in the wrong hands. Through her exclusive interviews with world-class experts in quantum technologies, Hannah explores the international quantum arms race between the US and China. She breaks down the implications of this 21st-century race and how a quantum future could change the very nature of humanity.

programme.title: John Simpson - 60 Years at the BBC
programme.desc: John Simpson looks back at his extraordinary 60-year career at the BBC - reporting on the biggest global stories of the era. In a frank, personal and revealing documentary, he reflects on the changing world he has witnessed: the revolution in Iran that seemed destined to fail, his brutal kidnapping in Beirut, the fall of the Berlin Wall, two wars in Iraq, the invasion of Afghanistan and a mind-altering trip up the Amazon. From the Broadcasting House newsroom in 1966 to World Affairs editor, he looks back at memorable encounters with inspiring leaders and cruel dictators - the figures who have shaped history, including Nelson Mandela, Margaret Thatcher, Saddam Hussein, Colonel Gaddafi and Volodymyr Zelensky. The programme also features his insights into the role of the BBC today and the challenges faced in the age of fake news.

In her quest to learn about the current state of animal communication, Professor Hannah Fry travels across the world, meeting Cash the talking dog in California and deciphering elephant rumbles in Nairobi. She looks into the question of whether the emerging ability to communicate with animals is one that should be exploited.

programme.title: Ira & Abby
programme.desc: A hastily married couple quickly devolve into a life of affairs, meddling parents, and therapy.

programme.title: Humpday
programme.desc: It's been a decade since Ben (Duplass) and Andrew (Leonard) were the bad boys of their college campus. Ben has settled down and found a job, wife, and home.

programme.title: God Bless America
programme.desc: Frank (Joel Murray) has had enough of the downward spiral of American culture. Divorced, recently fired, and possibly terminally ill, Frank feels he has nothing left to live for.

programme.title: The Lost City
